newsitem.title: UK: W.H.Smith plans sales to cut debt - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: W.H.Smith plans sales to cut debt - newspaper.

text.p: British retailer W.H. Smith Group is in talks to raise 40-50 million pounds ($67-$84 million) by selling some of its prime branches to help cut its debt level, the Sunday Times reported.
The newspaper said that the retailer, which has 105 million pounds of borrowings, expects to sell a quarter of its freehold properties, that are valued at a total of 195.3 million pounds.

W.H. Smith's new finance director, Keith Hamill, was quoted as saying: "We are looking at a series of sale-and-leasebacks to strengthen our financial positions...A series of deals is under negotiation."
The company may also decide to sell off more of its portfolio if demand for retail sites proves strong, the newspaper added.
W.H. Smith was not immediately available for comment.
